top_issues.issue: The lighter grey pillars can match the backdrop's value
top_issues.why: Where the pillar's grey-blue meets the same-value wall, the solid edge softens.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the lit faces, but make the backdrop cooler and hazier, or darken the pillar's shadow face for a clear silhouette.

top_issues.issue: Kindled is still mostly void
top_issues.why: Black is used for space rather than true void, so distant footing is hard to read.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep a faint hazed brick backdrop and add a few warm pools near the ledges.

per_shot.note: Wide-tracked logotype, glow and amber DESCEND button read well; darker scrim under the text sells the descent mood, though the rock is mostly lost to near-black and the warm rise from below is faint.
Clean, unobtrusive HUD; the thin fuel/hull bars and small labels are legible over the bright dusk sky but feel generic next to the stylised title.
The HUD stays out of the dark and leaves the lamp beam as the hero; the cargo list with ore icons reads clearly and its corner placement suits the mood.
Warm dark panel with amber corner brackets, clear hierarchy and a well-placed red debt line; the blurred world behind keeps the context; strong and on tone.
Quiet, sacred ending: soft glow behind OUT and good restraint; the italic body text is a little dim and small for its length.

top_issues.issue: The in-play HUD bars are flat, generic progress bars that share none of the title or shop's bracket/glow language
top_issues.why: The menus have a strong identity (amber brackets, tracked caps, warm glow); the gameplay HUD looks like a debug overlay next to them.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give fuel/hull a faceted or bracketed frame, a slight emissive edge and tracked labels that match the shop panel. Keep it small.

top_issues.issue: The title scrim crushes the rock under the logo to near-black, so the warm glow from below barely reads
top_issues.why: Reference 01 is about warm light rising up a dark shaft. Here the bottom glow is weak and the middle is uniform black.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Grade the scrim so it is darkest just behind the text and lets a stronger amber gradient rise from the bottom edge.

top_issues.issue: On the surface the top-left bars sit on a bright sky with only a thin backing
top_issues.why: The bar labels and numbers are small and low-contrast against the dusk gradient.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a subtle dark plate or a text shadow behind the bars on bright backgrounds.

top_issues.issue: The ending body copy is dim italic at a small size
top_issues.why: Six lines of narrative in light-grey italic on near-black are tiring to read at 1280 wide.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise its contrast slightly or set it upright with a bit more size or leading. Keep the glow on the headline only.

top_issues.issue: Glow is a hard square tile tint rather than bloom that lands on the rock around the ore.
top_issues.why: The art direction says emissives bloom softly and light lands on nearby surfaces; clipped squares read as UI highlight tiles and flatten the dark.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make the halo a radial falloff that is not clipped to the tile, and add a small point light or vertex tint so the adjacent rock faces pick up the ore colour.

top_issues.issue: Nacre has a crystal-cluster silhouette rather than a ribbed shell or fan.
top_issues.why: With a pale halo and spiky points it collides with frostbloom, silver and diamond in the pale group.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build a scalloped fan from 3–5 stacked ribbed arcs on a slate base, with a pearly pink-teal sheen and a weaker glow.

top_issues.issue: Iron is too dark and low-contrast against the host rock.
top_issues.why: Iron has no glow, so it must read through gunmetal-blue colour and specular; in the lineup it nearly vanishes.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Lift the blue-grey albedo, add a bright rim or specular edge on the cube faces and a couple of blue glints; keep the shape blocky.

top_issues.issue: Ores float in the tile with tiny or missing host-rock bases.
top_issues.why: The references always show ore erupting from matte dark rock; without a base the ore looks pasted on rather than embedded.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each ore a consistent dark matte rock seat that the ore grows from, and let the glow pool at that base.

top_issues.issue: Pale ores are separated only by shape, because they share a similar white or grey halo.
top_issues.why: Silver, diamond and frostbloom all use similar pale glows, so at 40–60 px the shape alone carries identity.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Drop silver's glow to near zero and rely on specular, push diamond to cool ice-blue with a sparkle glint, and push frostbloom further toward lavender.
